newsitem.title: GERMANY: CONDOR SELLS TWO DC10-30 AIRCRAFT.
newsitem.headline: CONDOR SELLS TWO DC10-30 AIRCRAFT.

text.p: Condor Flugdienst GmbH, the holiday airline unit of Deutsche Lufthansa AG, said it had sold two McDonnell Douglas DC10-30 aircraft to an American leasing company.
Managing director Franz Schoiber said the aircraft, taken over from Lufthansa three years ago, had been disposed of due to moderate demand for the forthcoming 1998-98 winter season.
He said the purchaser was linked to Continental Airlines but did not name it or give a sale price.
Speaking at a news conference, Schoiber said only: "We sold the two DC-10s for a good price."
Under a planned 1.4 billion mark fleet renewal, Condor planned to operate a flexible fleet based around the new Boeing 757-300 and the smaller Airbus A320-200, he added.
The airline would be the launch customer for 12 Boeing 757-300 aircraft with 252 seats which would replace its 370-seat DC10-30 fleet from spring 1999, Schoiber said.
A planned low-cost "Condor Berlin" subsidiary, which will probably be based in Berlin, should launch in summer 1998 with the first three of six ordered Airbus A320-200 aircraft.
These 168-seat aircraft would replace four leased Boeing 737-300s due for return to charter carrier Germania in 1998 and would serve small regional markets.
"The B757 is simply too big. We want to go into new markets with a cost-efficient A320," Schoiber said.
